speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Government regularly reviews Singapore’s criminal justice policies, including our policy on caning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will provide an update if there are changes to this policy.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have a supplementary question, but before that, on a point of elucidation, the focus of my question is whether using the age of 50 is a rational and reasonable differentiating measure to distinguish between those who will be visited with a minimum mandatory caning sentence for committing serious sexual offences on one hand, and those who have committed such offences but escape it because they are above 50.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: With your leave, Sir, may I be allowed to use the screen on a point of information?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The life expectancy of persons then, you would see, Sir, was about 48.5 years, in around 1900.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, quite clearly, if I could say it, age 50 then would have been age about 80-plus now.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, my question to the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary is, is there still a basis to maintain age of 50 as a differentiating measure?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I take the point that the Member has made that health conditions have changed since then.
